toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise in missed appointments at Corrie Lane is real. It is not mainly a recording artefact: an audit found miscoding explains only about 0.5 points of the 13.4%. It is not the bus change or the season either. Eastgate, which shares the catchment and the bus route, stayed at about 8%, and Corrie Lane was about 8% a year earlier. Front-desk confirmation calls did not stop. Calls to the minor-procedures list were 93% before and 91% after, so the staff warnings should not go ahead. Hiding the figure from the board would also be a mistake.

The cause is almost certainly the Tidewell configuration. Two changes happened together on 3 March across all templates: the near-date reminder was replaced by a 7-day one, and booking lead times went from a median of about 19 days to about 52. Nothing in the data separates the two, and lead-time outcomes can't be extracted for about 10 weeks. I'm fairly sure of the rest and unsure which of these two matters more.

Next step: run the randomised 8-week test of a 48-hour reminder on half the templates, and ask the vendor for the booking-timestamp extract now. Don't change the booking horizon or the whole clinic's configuration until the test reports.
